claims.text: First tests: CBC with platelet count, peripheral smear, PT and aPTT.
claims.quote: The initial tests are: Complete blood count (CBC) with platelet count Peripheral blood smear Prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)

claims.text: Add renal and liver function tests when a bleeding disorder is suspected.
claims.quote: A peripheral blood smear, complete blood count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, and renal and liver function tests should be obtained in patients with an abnormal ISTH-BAT score or in whom a bleeding disorder is suspected.

claims.text: Prolonged PT or aPTT: repeat after a 1:1 mix with normal plasma; failure to correct suggests an inhibitor rather than a factor deficiency.
claims.quote: For determining whether prolongation reflects a deficiency of one or more clotting factor or the presence of an inhibitor, the test is repeated after mixing the patient’s plasma with normal plasma in a 1:1 ratio. Because this mixture contains at least 50% of normal levels of all coagulation factors, failure of the mixture to correct the prolongation almost completely suggests the presence of an inhibitor in patient plasma.

claims.text: Bleeding time is not reliable enough to use.
claims.quote: The bleeding time test is not sufficiently reproducible to be reliable for clinical decision-making.

claims.text: Hematology referral when suspicion of a bleeding disorder stays high.
claims.quote: Thus, if suspicion of a bleeding disorder is high, evaluation by a hematologist is warranted.
